metadata.title: TSX set for higher open as Micron earnings revive global technology sector

content.text:
Investing.com -- Canadian equity markets appeared poised for a positive open on Thursday after strong corporate earnings breathed new life into the global artificial intelligence trade. The anticipation of a higher open follows a downbeat Wednesday session where the benchmark S&P/TSX Composite fell 191.29 points, or 0.55%, to close at 34,736.09, while the S&P/TSX 60 dropped 0.30% to finish at 2,049.68.
Ahead of the opening bell, S&P/TSX 60 Futures rose 0.39% to C$2,062.4.
Micron Crushes Expectations on AI Demand
Memory-chip maker Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU) crushed Wall Street expectations in its fiscal third quarter and issued significantly stronger-than-expected guidance for the current quarter, sending shares up about 18.5% in pre-market trading as investors cheered continued AI-driven demand for memory chips. For the quarter ended May 28, Micron reported adjusted earnings of $25.11 per share on record revenue of $41.46 billion, comfortably beating analyst estimates of $20.49 per share and $35.69 billion.
Looking ahead, the chipmaker forecast fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $49 billion to $51 billion and earnings per share of $30.00 to $32.00, well above the respective analyst consensuses of $43.24 billion and $25.31. Management also pushed back against margin peak concerns by forecasting an 86% gross margin for the upcoming quarter and indicating on the post-earnings conference call that memory supply constraints show little sign of easing.
U.S. Markets Move Sharply Higher
U.S. stock index futures rose sharply in Thursday premarket trade with technology and chipmaking shares rallying after hours following strong guidance from Micron and Qualcomm. In morning action, Nasdaq 100 Futures surged 2.32% to 30,199.00, while S&P 500 Futures gained 0.81% to 7,488.25 and Dow Jones Futures edged up 0.27% to 52,422.00.
These futures gains materialized after a mostly negative session on Wall Street, where investors remained skittish towards tech following a major wipeout in the sector this week. The strong corporate outlooks helped reverse that negative momentum and restore confidence among major tech investors.
Gold Rebounds From Multi-Month Lows
Gold prices rebounded slightly on Thursday, clawing back some ground close to their lowest levels in more than seven months. Despite the minor bounce, a strong U.S. dollar and growing expectations of further Federal Reserve monetary tightening continue to erode demand for the non-yielding metal.
In electronic trading, Gold Futures moved up 0.51% to trade at $4,029.27 per ounce. Meanwhile, XAU/USD prices also edged higher, rising 0.35% to sit at $4,013.12.
